The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let the final board be listed in nondecreasing order (counting repetitions) as

\[
x_1\le x_2\le \cdots \le x_{2100}.
\]

We need \(x_{2026}\).

For a prime \(p\), let \(v_p(n)\) be the exponent of \(p\) in \(n\).  
When Mark replaces \(a,b\) by \(\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\), the pair of \(p\)-adic exponents \((v_p(a),v_p(b))\) is replaced by

\[
(\min(v_p(a),v_p(b)),\max(v_p(a),v_p(b))).
\]

So for every prime \(p\), the multiset of all \(p\)-adic exponents on the board is invariant.

At the stopping moment, no move can change the board. That means every pair of numbers on the board is comparable by divisibility: for any two board numbers \(a,b\), either \(a\mid b\) or \(b\mid a\). Otherwise \(\gcd(a,b)<\min(a,b)\) and \(\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)>\max(a,b)\), so the board would change.

Thus the final numbers form a divisibility chain:

\[
x_1\mid x_2\mid \cdots \mid x_{2100}.
\]

Therefore, for each prime \(p\), the sequence

\[
v_p(x_1),v_p(x_2),\dots,v_p(x_{2100})
\]

is nondecreasing. Since the multiset of these exponents is invariant, \(v_p(x_i)\) must be the \(i\)-th smallest \(p\)-adic exponent among the original numbers \(1,2,\dots,2100\).

Now we want \(i=2026\). There are

\[
2100-2026+1=75
\]

numbers from \(x_{2026}\) through \(x_{2100}\). Thus for a prime \(p\),

\[
v_p(x_{2026})\ge r
\]

if and only if at least \(75\) of the original numbers \(1,2,\dots,2100\) are divisible by \(p^r\). The number of such original numbers is

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^r}\right\rfloor.
\]

So the exponent of \(p\) in \(x_{2026}\) is the largest \(r\) such that

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^r}\right\rfloor\ge 75.
\]

Since \(2100=75\cdot 28\), this is equivalent to

\[
p^r\le 28.
\]

Now list the possible primes:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
p & v_p(x_{2026}) \\ \hline
2 & 4 \quad (2^4=16\le 28<32)\\
3 & 3 \quad (3^3=27\le 28<81)\\
5 & 2 \quad (5^2=25\le 28<125)\\
7,11,13,17,19,23 & 1\\
p\ge 29 & 0
\end{array}
\]

Thus

\[
x_{2026}=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]

The number of positive divisors of \(x_{2026}\) is

\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
